_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Malta covering megalithic temples (~3600 BCE, oldest free-standing structures in world), Phoenician/Carthaginian/Roman rule, Arab conquest (870 CE, Maltese language roots), Norman conquest 1091, Knights Hospitaller/Order of St. John (1530-1798, Great Siege 1565), French occupation (Napoleon 1798), British Crown Colony (1800-1964), George Cross (WWII), independence 1964, Republic 1974, EU 2004.

religion.note: Most Catholic country in Europe; Catholicism in constitution; patron saint village festas (band clubs, fireworks, competitive, define community identity); St. Paul's shipwreck tradition (Acts 28, apostolic Christianity); abortion only legalised 2023 (last EU country); divorce only allowed since 2011; Knights of Malta Catholic legacy

ethnic_groups.name: Maltese
ethnic_groups.notes: Unique Semitic-Romance heritage; Maltese language (Semitic/Arabic root with heavy Italian/English layers, only Semitic language written in Latin script); island identity strong; festa/village loyalty; Knight heritage pride; diaspora in Australia (~190k, Melbourne largest Maltese community outside Malta)

ethnic_groups.name: British
ethnic_groups.notes: Colonial legacy; retirement community; English widely spoken; British cultural influence

ethnic_groups.name: Italian
ethnic_groups.notes: Historical ties (Italian was elite language until 1930s); Sicilian proximity (80km)

ethnic_groups.name: Other EU
ethnic_groups.notes: Bulgarian, Romanian, German; EU free movement; iGaming industry workers

ethnic_groups.name: Non-EU
ethnic_groups.notes: Indian, Filipino, Serbian, Libyan, Eritrean; massive population growth (23% increase 2014-2024, fastest in EU); construction boom; TCN workers controversy; Daphne Caruana Galizia murder linked to corruption; Mediterranean boat migrants (SAR zone)

country_profile.notes_unique: Megalithic temples (Ggantija, Hagar Qim, Mnajdra; ~3600-2500 BCE, older than Stonehenge and Egyptian pyramids, oldest free-standing stone structures on Earth); Great Siege 1565 (Knights of St. John held Malta against Ottoman Empire/Suleiman the Magnificent, 40k Ottoman troops vs 6k, defining moment of Christian-Muslim confrontation in Mediterranean, Valletta built as celebration); George Cross 1942 (King George VI awarded entire island for WWII heroism, most bombed place in war, on national flag); Maltese language (only Semitic language in EU, Arabic-derived substrate with Sicilian/Italian/English superstate, written in Latin script); smallest EU member state; Valletta (smallest EU capital, entire city UNESCO World Heritage); Knights of Malta/Order of St. John (1530-1798, built fortifications, hospitals, art); Daphne Caruana Galizia (investigative journalist assassinated 2017 by car bomb, Panama Papers/corruption, national crisis, three men convicted, political fallout); iGaming capital of Europe (regulatory framework attracted ~300 companies); Golden passport scheme (EU criticism, suspended); 3 UNESCO World Heritage sites; film location (Game of Thrones, Gladiator, Troy)

comparative_rankings._note: Country position relative to continent and global. 'rank' = 1 is best/largest.

current_leader.name: Robert Abela
current_leader.title: Prime Minister
current_leader.notes: Labour Party; lawyer; son of former president George Abela; succeeded Muscat (who resigned over Caruana Galizia murder accountability); re-elected March 2022 (strong majority); economic growth focus; corruption scrutiny continues; Moneyval grey-listing removed; pro-EU

head_of_state.name: Myriam Spiteri Debono
head_of_state.title: President
head_of_state.notes: First female president; former Speaker of the House; lawyer; Labour-nominated; largely ceremonial role

former_leaders.name: Joseph Muscat
former_leaders.notes: Labour; youngest PM (39); economic boom; same-sex marriage 2017 (Catholic Malta!); but Caruana Galizia assassination scandal (journalist murdered 2017, chief of staff/minister implicated, Panama Papers connections); resigned January 2020 under pressure; charged with corruption 2023

former_leaders.name: Lawrence Gonzi
former_leaders.notes: Nationalist Party; EU accession 2004; Euro adoption 2008; divorce referendum 2011 (yes vote despite Church opposition); lost to Muscat amid austerity

former_leaders.name: Dom Mintoff
former_leaders.notes: Labour; dominant, polarising figure; closed British military bases (1979); Non-Aligned Movement; socialist policies; confrontational with Church (interdiction crisis 1960s); built welfare state; cult of personality; love-or-hate figure; died 2012

910.name: Megalithic Temples and Prehistoric Malta
910.description: Malta's extraordinary prehistoric period, home to the oldest freestanding structures in the world — megalithic temples predating the Egyptian pyramids and Stonehenge — and the mysterious collapse of the temple-building civilization.

sub_clusters.name: First Settlers and Temple Builders
sub_clusters.description: The arrival of Neolithic settlers from Sicily, the construction of the Ġgantija, Ħaġar Qim, Mnajdra, and Tarxien temples (the oldest freestanding structures on Earth), the Ħal Saflieni Hypogeum, and the mysterious collapse of the temple period.
key_events: Construction of Ġgantija temples on Gozo — world's oldest freestanding structures (c. 3600 BC)
Construction of Ħaġar Qim and Mnajdra temple complexes (c. 3200 BC)
